rows.reason: The self-reported 84 km pilot result supports the weaker lower bound of 70 km for the same week.
Both clauses weaken the source quantities and retain the personal contribution and 2024 setting.
The candidate and job clauses preserve their different evidence types; the relevance judgment follows their shared duty.
The paper subset is explicitly 31 and the total is 43, both self-reported for the same month.
The recommendation reflects the stated sandbox trial and explicit absence of deployment.
Certification has a stated issuer, while the demo count is explicitly self-reported and conservatively lowered.
It attributes scoring to the candidate and reserves final decisions for the chair.
The answer uses the past schedule as history and explicitly leaves present availability unresolved.
Two observed weekends per quarter supports a lower bound of one, restricted to 2024.
Eighteen months exceeds a year, and the source explicitly excludes purchase approval.
The signed log supplies direct evidence for the same narrow activity named by the job.
Both the recommended inclusion and exclusion follow the candidate’s limited self-report.
Attendance is supported. Not taking the trainer assessment does not establish certificate status; earning the certificate is unsupported by this source.
A 14-form trial does not support validation across the unprocessed collection.
The first clause is accurate team output; the second contradicts the explicit individual role.
The historical escalation is supported; the source explicitly ends on-call duty in 2021.
A forecast for an unimplemented route cannot support a guaranteed realized saving.
Platform operation is supported, but the candidate says live captioning is unavailable.
“On call for shifts” may mean covered the shifts or remained reachable outside them.
rows.review_reason: Clarify whether the answer means support while scheduled or availability between shifts.
